source.text: Ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις πάλιν πολλοῦ ὄχλου ὄντος καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων τί φάγωσιν, προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς λέγει αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: In those the days again great crowd being and not having what they might eat, having called to [him] the disciples he says to them,

en.L: In those days, when again [there] was a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called the disciples to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and says to them,
en.B: During those days a large crowd had gathered again, and there was no food for them. So Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said to them,
en.R: Around that time another big crowd came together around Jesus. The people had run out of food. So Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers over and said to them,

vi.L: Trong những ngày ấy, khi lại có đoàn dân đông và họ không có gì để ăn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi các môn đồ đến [với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] và nói với họ:
vi.B: Trong những ngày ấy, lại có một đoàn dân rất đông tụ tập, và họ không có gì ăn. Vì vậy, Đức Giê-xu gọi các môn đồ đến và nói với họ:
vi.R: Khoảng thời gian đó, lại có một đoàn dân rất đông tụ họp quanh Đức Giê-xu. Mọi người đã hết thức ăn. Vì vậy Đức Giê-xu gọi các môn đồ lại và nói với họ:

ko.L: 그 무렵에 다시 큰 무리가 있었는데, 그들에게 먹을 것이 없었으므로, 그분이 제자들을 [가까이] 불러 그들에게 말씀하신다.
ko.B: 그 무렵에 또 큰 무리가 모여들었는데, 그들에게는 먹을 것이 없었다. 예수께서 제자들을 가까이 부르시고 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 그 무렵에 또 많은 사람이 예수 주위에 모였다. 사람들은 가져온 음식이 다 떨어졌다. 그래서 예수께서 제자들을 가까이 부르시고 말씀하셨다.

es.L: En aquellos días, como otra vez había una gran multitud y no tenían qué comer, llamó a los discípulos y les dice:
es.B: Por aquellos días se reunió otra vez una gran multitud, y no tenían nada que comer. Entonces Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dijo:
es.R: Por ese tiempo, otra vez se juntó mucha gente alrededor de Jesús. Ya no les quedaba comida. Entonces Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dijo:

fr.L: En ces jours-là, comme il y avait de nouveau une foule nombreuse et qu’ils n’avaient rien à manger, ayant appelé les disciples, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit :
fr.B: En ces jours-là, une grande foule s’était de nouveau rassemblée, et elle n’avait rien à manger. Jésus appela alors {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et leur dit :
fr.R: À cette époque, une autre grande foule s’est rassemblée autour de Jésus. Les gens n’avaient plus rien à manger. Alors Jésus a appelé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et leur a dit :

sw.L: Katika siku zile, tena kulipokuwa na umati mkubwa nao hawana kitu cha kula, akiisha kuwaita wanafunzi [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], anawaambia,
sw.B: Katika siku hizo umati mkubwa ulikusanyika tena, nao hawakuwa na chakula. Basi Yesu akawaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawaambia,
sw.R: Wakati huo umati mwingine mkubwa ulikusanyika kumzunguka Yesu. Watu walikuwa wamemaliza chakula chao. Basi Yesu akawaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawaambia,

decisions.choice: again a great crowd: a second large crowd, like the one in 6:34
decisions.reason: The word for again points back to the earlier feeding. Mark tells a second, similar meal in a different place, the Gentile region of the Ten Towns where Jesus was in 7:31.

decisions.choice: again a great crowd, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a single word meaning a very great crowd, without again. The SBLGNT reads again with great, as the older manuscripts do. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past, here and in 8:6, 8:12, 8:17, 8:19-20, 8:22, 8:29 and 8:33.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L) for the present "says"
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present ("says", 8:1, 8:12, 8:17, 8:19-20, 8:29, 8:33). Vietnamese verbs have no tense, so Literal keeps the vivid present by leaving out "đã", as the Vietnamese John does; Balanced and Readable narrate plainly.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("말씀하신다", "말한다", "온다"), through chapter 8
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (8:1, 8:6, 8:12, 8:17, 8:19, 8:20, 8:22, 8:29, 8:33); Balanced and Readable use the past. Recorded once for the chapter.

decisions.choice: present tense (L); past tense (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:12: Literal keeps Mark's present ("dice"); Balanced and Readable use the past. This applies throughout the chapter. Plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros setting, and every pronoun for Jesus that Spanish writes as a separate word takes the deity_pronoun setting, by the rule set for Mark at 1:2.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B), with Literal keeping Mark’s present tense ("il leur dit", "ils viennent", "ils lui disent") and using the passé simple elsewhere; passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole of Mark 8. The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken and school French. Literal keeps the present wherever Mark tells a past event in the present (8:1, 6, 12, 17, 19, 20, 22, 29, 33).

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawaambia); past at Balanced and Readable (akawaambia)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present (meaning decision). Literal keeps it, as in the earlier chapters; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past with -li- and -ka-, as written Swahili narrative does. This holds for the whole of chapter 8.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (kwake, wake, yangu, mimi)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in John and the earlier chapters of Mark: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb ("akawaita", "akawaambia"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer setting spans than English in this chapter.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi (disciples) at every level
decisions.reason: As in John and the earlier chapters of Mark, "wanafunzi" is plain enough for Readable, where the English Readable says "followers".

source.text: Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν·

records.literal_gloss: I have compassion on the crowd, because already days three they remain with me and not they have anything they might eat;

en.L: "I have compassion on the crowd, because they have already remained with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three days and do not have anything to eat;
en.B: "My heart goes out to these people. They have been with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for three days now, and they have nothing left to eat.
en.R: "I feel sorry for these people. They have stayed with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for three days, and now they have nothing to eat.

vi.L: "Ta thương xót đoàn dân này, vì họ đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ba ngày rồi và không có gì để ăn;
vi.B: "Ta động lòng thương xót những người này. Họ đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ba ngày rồi, mà nay không còn gì để ăn.
vi.R: "Ta thương những người này quá. Họ đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ba ngày, và bây giờ họ không còn gì để ăn.

ko.L: "내가 무리를 불쌍히 여긴다. 그들이 벌써 사흘 동안 나와 함께 머물러 있었는데, 먹을 것이 없기 때문이다.
ko.B: "이 사람들이 참 가엾구나. 벌써 사흘이나 나와 함께 있었는데, 이제 먹을 것이 없다.
ko.R: "이 사람들이 불쌍하다. 사흘 동안이나 나와 함께 있었는데, 이제는 먹을 것이 하나도 없다.

es.L: «Tengo compasión de la multitud, porque ya hace tres días que permanecen conmigo y no tienen qué comer;
es.B: «Siento compasión por esta gente. Ya llevan tres días conmigo y no tienen nada que comer.
es.R: «Me da pena esta gente. Han estado conmigo tres días, y ahora no tienen nada que comer.

fr.L: « J’ai compassion de la foule, car voilà déjà trois jours qu’ils restent avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ils n’ont rien à manger ;
fr.B: « Je suis plein de compassion pour cette foule. Voilà déjà trois jours qu’ils sont avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ils n’ont plus rien à manger.
fr.R: « J’ai pitié de ces gens. Ils sont restés avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} pendant trois jours, et maintenant ils n’ont plus rien à manger.

sw.L: "Ninauhurumia umati, kwa sababu tayari siku tatu wamekaa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, wala hawana kitu cha kula;
sw.B: "Ninawaonea huruma sana watu hawa. Wamekuwa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} kwa siku tatu sasa, nao hawana chochote kilichobaki cha kula.
sw.R: "Ninawahurumia watu hawa. Wamekaa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} kwa siku tatu, na sasa hawana chochote cha kula.

decisions.choice: have compassion: be moved deep inside with pity
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for the inner parts, where people felt strong feeling. It is used of Jesus at 1:41 and at the first feeding (6:34).

decisions.choice: already three days: they have stayed so long that their food is gone
decisions.reason: The point is how long they have kept listening to him in a lonely place.

decisions.choice: my heart goes out to
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English phrase for deep pity.

decisions.choice: "thương xót" (L); "động lòng thương xót" (B); "thương ... quá" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is pity felt deep inside (meaning decision). "Động lòng" (the heart is moved) gives that depth at Balanced; Readable uses the everyday "thương".

decisions.choice: "불쌍히 여긴다" (L); "가엾구나" (B); "불쌍하다" (R) for the compassion of Jesus
decisions.reason: Plain current words for being moved with pity; "긍휼" is an older church word that new readers may not know.

decisions.choice: siento compasión (B); me da pena (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday Spanish for being moved with pity (meaning decision m1); "me da pena" means "I feel sorry", not "I am ashamed", in the Spanish of both sides of the Atlantic. "Conmigo" is one word and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: "je suis plein de compassion" (B); "j’ai pitié" (R); "j’ai compassion" (L)
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of being moved deep inside (meaning decision). Balanced gives the depth with "plein de"; Readable uses the everyday "avoir pitié", which in French carries no contempt.

decisions.choice: Ninawaonea huruma sana (I feel great pity for)
alternatives: Moyo wangu unawaonea huruma (my heart pities)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is pity felt deep inside (meaning decision). "Kuonea huruma" with "sana" says that in plain Swahili; the picture of the heart, which the English Balanced uses, adds nothing in Swahili, where "huruma" is already a feeling of the heart.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀπολύσω αὐτοὺς νήστεις εἰς οἶκον αὐτῶν, ἐκλυθήσονται ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ· καί τινες αὐτῶν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἥκασιν.

records.literal_gloss: and if I send away them hungry to [the] home of them, they will faint on the road; and some of them from far away have come.

en.L: and if I send them away hungry to their homes, they will faint on the road; and some of them have come from far away."
en.B: Send them home without food, and they will collapse on the road. Some of them have traveled a long way."
en.R: If they have to go home hungry, they will become weak and fall down on the way. Some of them have come from far away."

vi.L: và nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho họ về nhà mà còn đói, họ sẽ kiệt sức dọc đường; mà có mấy người trong số họ đã từ xa đến."
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho họ về nhà mà không ăn gì, họ sẽ ngất xỉu dọc đường. Có những người đã đi từ rất xa đến."
vi.R: Nếu họ phải về nhà mà bụng đói, họ sẽ kiệt sức và ngã quỵ dọc đường. Có người đã từ nơi xa đến."

ko.L: 내가 그들을 굶은 채로 그들의 집으로 돌려보내면, 그들이 길에서 기진할 것이다. 그리고 그들 가운데 어떤 사람들은 멀리서 왔다."
ko.B: 그들을 굶긴 채로 집으로 돌려보내면, 가다가 길에서 쓰러질 것이다. 이 가운데에는 먼 데서 온 사람들도 있다."
ko.R: 배고픈 채로 집에 돌아가게 하면, 가는 길에 힘이 빠져 쓰러질 것이다. 아주 먼 곳에서 온 사람들도 있다."

es.L: y si los despido en ayunas a sus casas, desfallecerán en el camino; y algunos de ellos han venido de lejos».
es.B: Si los mando a sus casas sin comer, se van a desmayar por el camino. Algunos de ellos han venido de muy lejos».
es.R: Si tienen que irse a casa con hambre, se van a debilitar y a caer por el camino. Algunos de ellos han venido desde lejos».

fr.L: et si je les renvoie à jeun chez eux, ils défailliront en chemin ; et certains d’entre eux sont venus de loin. »
fr.B: Si je les renvoie chez eux sans qu’ils aient mangé, ils vont s’effondrer en route. Certains d’entre eux sont venus de loin. »
fr.R: S’ils rentrent chez eux sans avoir mangé, ils vont perdre leurs forces et tomber en chemin. Certains sont venus de loin. »

sw.L: na nikiwaaga waende nyumbani kwao wakiwa na njaa, watazimia njiani; na baadhi yao wamekuja kutoka mbali."
sw.B: Nikiwaaga waende nyumbani bila kula, wataishiwa nguvu njiani. Baadhi yao wamesafiri kutoka mbali."
sw.R: Wakilazimika kwenda nyumbani wakiwa na njaa, watachoka na kuanguka njiani. Baadhi yao wametoka mbali."

decisions.choice: faint: give out from weakness and hunger
decisions.reason: The verb means to become slack or exhausted.

decisions.choice: from far away: perhaps a hint that Gentiles are among the crowd
decisions.reason: The scene is in Gentile country (7:31), and in the Scriptures those far off can mean the nations (Joshua 9:6; Isaiah 60:4). Mark may mean no more than the distance.

decisions.choice: and some of them, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts join the clause with a word meaning for, making it a reason. The sense is close either way. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

source.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι Πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπ’ ἐρημίας;

records.literal_gloss: And answered him the disciples of him that, From where these will be able anyone here to satisfy with bread in a desolate place?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "From where will anyone be able to satisfy these [people] with bread here in a desolate place?"
en.B: His disciples replied, "Out here in this empty country, where could anyone find bread enough to fill all these people?"
en.R: His followers answered, "We are far from any town. How could anyone get enough bread here to feed all these people?"

vi.L: Và các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ai có thể lấy đâu ra bánh ở đây, nơi hoang vắng, để cho những người này ăn no?"
vi.B: Các môn đồ thưa: "Ở nơi hoang vắng này, ai có thể kiếm đâu ra đủ bánh cho ngần ấy người ăn no?"
vi.R: Các môn đồ trả lời: "Ở đây xa mọi làng mạc. Làm sao ai kiếm được đủ bánh để cho tất cả những người này ăn?"

ko.L: 그러자 그분의 제자들이 그분께 대답하였다. "여기 이 광야에서 누가 어디서 빵을 구해 이 사람들을 배불리 먹일 수 있겠습니까?"
ko.B: 제자들이 대답하였다. "이런 외딴 들판에서 누가 어디서 빵을 구해 이 많은 사람을 배불리 먹일 수 있겠습니까?"
ko.R: 제자들이 대답했다. "여기는 마을에서 멀리 떨어진 곳입니다. 이 많은 사람을 먹일 빵을 어디서 구할 수 있겠습니까?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿De dónde podrá alguien saciar de pan a estos aquí, en un lugar despoblado?».
es.B: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Aquí, en este lugar despoblado, ¿de dónde podría alguien sacar pan suficiente para dar de comer a toda esta gente?».
es.R: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contestaron: «Estamos lejos de cualquier pueblo. ¿Cómo va a conseguir alguien aquí pan suficiente para alimentar a toda esta gente?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « D’où quelqu’un pourra-t-il rassasier de pains ces [gens]-ci, ici, dans un désert ? »
fr.B: Ses disciples répondirent : « Ici, dans cet endroit désert, où pourrait-on trouver assez de pain pour nourrir tous ces gens ? »
fr.R: Ses disciples ont répondu : « Nous sommes loin de toute ville. Comment trouver ici assez de pain pour nourrir tous ces gens ? »

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamjibu, "Mtu ataweza kutoka wapi kuwashibisha hawa kwa mikate hapa nyikani?"
sw.B: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakajibu, "Huku nyikani, mtu angepata wapi mikate ya kutosha kuwashibisha watu wote hawa?"
sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakajibu, "Tuko mbali na mji wowote. Mtu anawezaje kupata mikate ya kutosha hapa ya kuwalisha watu wote hawa?"

decisions.choice: desolate place: open country far from towns
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the lonely place of the first feeding (6:35). It recalls Israel fed in the wilderness (Exodus 16).

decisions.choice: a question that sees no way to feed them
alternatives: a request for Jesus to act
decisions.reason: The disciples have seen the first feeding (6:35-44), yet they speak as though they had not. Jesus takes this up in 8:17-21.

decisions.choice: we are far from any town
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lonely place means for the problem.

decisions.choice: "광야" (L); "외딴 들판" (B); "마을에서 멀리 떨어진 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: The place is open country far from towns, not a sandy desert; "사막" would mislead. Balanced and Readable say what kind of place it is.

decisions.choice: mkate, mikate (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in John 6: the chapter turns on bread, from the loaves of the feeding to the one loaf in the boat (8:14-21). "Mkate" keeps it one word at every level; "chakula" (food) is kept for Readable in 8:14, where the English Readable also says "food".

source.text: καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτούς· Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους;

records.literal_gloss: And he was asking them, How many have you loaves?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "How many loaves do you have?"
en.B: He asked them, "How many loaves have you got?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves of bread do you have?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Các con có mấy cái bánh?"
vi.B: Ngài hỏi họ: "Các con có bao nhiêu cái bánh?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi: "Các con có mấy ổ bánh?"

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 물으셨다. "너희에게 빵이 몇 개 있느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 물으셨다. "빵이 몇 개 있느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들에게 물으셨다. "너희에게 빵이 몇 개 있느냐?"

es.L: Y les preguntaba: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».
es.B: Les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demandait : « Combien de pains avez-vous ? »
fr.B: Il leur demanda : « Combien avez-vous de pains ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé : « Combien de pains avez-vous ? »

sw.L: Naye akawauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"
sw.B: Akawauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"
sw.R: Yesu akawauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat rounds of bread
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in small, flat rounds, one or two of which made a meal for a person.

decisions.choice: "cái bánh" (L, B); "ổ bánh" (R) for "loaves"
decisions.reason: "Cái bánh" is the counting form the Vietnamese John uses for the loaves (John 6:9-13). Readable says "ổ bánh" (a loaf), which makes plain that this is bread.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά.

records.literal_gloss: And they said, Seven.

en.L: And they said, "Seven."
en.B: "Seven," they answered.
en.R: They said, "Seven."

vi.L: Và họ thưa: "Bảy."
vi.B: "Bảy cái," họ thưa.
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Bảy ổ."

ko.L: 그들이 말하였다. "일곱 [개입니다]."
ko.B: "일곱 개 있습니다" 하고 그들이 대답하였다.
ko.R: 제자들이 대답했다. "일곱 개 있습니다."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Siete».
es.B: «Siete», respondieron.
es.R: Ellos dijeron: «Siete».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Sept. »
fr.B: « Sept », répondirent-ils.
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Sept. »

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Saba."
sw.B: "Saba," wakajibu.
sw.R: Wakasema, "Saba."

decisions.choice: seven: a number of fullness
alternatives: a count with no further meaning
decisions.reason: The first feeding began with five loaves and ended with twelve baskets. Here there are seven loaves and seven baskets (8:8). Seven can stand for completeness, but Mark gives no explanation.

source.text: καὶ παραγγέλλει τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν καὶ παρέθηκαν τῷ ὄχλῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And he directs the crowd to recline on the ground; and having taken the seven loaves, having given thanks he broke and was giving to the disciples of him that they might set before, and they set before the crowd.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} directs the crowd to recline on the ground; and having taken the seven loaves [and] given thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [them] and was giving [them] to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples so that they would serve [them], and they served the crowd.
en.B: He had the crowd sit on the ground. Taking the seven loaves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave thanks, broke them, and kept handing them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to pass around, and they served them to the crowd.
en.R: Jesus told the people to sit on the ground. He took the seven loaves and thanked God for them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the bread into pieces and gave it to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to hand out. They gave it to the people.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} truyền cho đoàn dân ngồi xuống đất; và cầm lấy bảy cái bánh, tạ ơn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bẻ ra và trao cho các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để họ dọn ra, và họ dọn ra cho đoàn dân.
vi.B: Ngài bảo đoàn dân ngồi xuống đất. Ngài cầm lấy bảy cái bánh, tạ ơn, bẻ ra rồi cứ trao cho các môn đồ để họ phân phát, và họ phát cho đoàn dân.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo mọi người ngồi xuống đất. Ngài cầm bảy ổ bánh và cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bẻ bánh ra và đưa cho các môn đồ để họ phát cho mọi người. Các môn đồ phát bánh cho dân chúng.

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 무리에게 땅에 앉으라고 명하신다. 그리고 빵 일곱 개를 들고 감사 기도를 드리신 뒤에 떼어서, 자기 제자들에게 주시며 나누어 주게 하셨다. 그러자 그들이 무리에게 나누어 주었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 무리에게 땅에 앉으라고 하셨다. 그리고 빵 일곱 개를 들고 감사 기도를 드리신 다음, 떼어서 제자들에게 계속 건네주시며 나누어 주게 하셨다. 제자들은 그것을 무리에게 나누어 주었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 사람들에게 땅에 앉으라고 말씀하셨다. 그리고 빵 일곱 개를 손에 들고 하나님께 감사 기도를 드리셨다. 그다음에 빵을 떼어 제자들에게 주시며 사람들에게 나누어 주라고 하셨다. 제자들은 빵을 사람들에게 나누어 주었다.

es.L: Y manda a la multitud recostarse en el suelo; y tomando los siete panes, habiendo dado gracias, [los] partió y [los] iba dando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que [los] sirvieran, y [los] sirvieron a la multitud.
es.B: Mandó a la multitud que se sentara en el suelo. Tomó los siete panes, dio gracias, los partió y se los iba dando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que los repartieran, y ellos los repartieron a la multitud.
es.R: Jesús le dijo a la gente que se sentara en el suelo. Tomó los siete panes y le dio gracias a Dios por ellos. Luego partió el pan en pedazos y se lo dio a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que lo repartieran. Ellos se lo dieron a la gente.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ordonne à la foule de s’allonger par terre ; et ayant pris les sept pains, ayant rendu grâce, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [les] rompit, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [les] donnait à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples pour qu’ils [les] servent ; et ils [les] servirent à la foule.
fr.B: Il fit asseoir la foule par terre. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les sept pains, rendit grâce, les rompit, et les donna au fur et à mesure à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples pour qu’ils les distribuent ; et ils les servirent à la foule.
fr.R: Jésus a dit aux gens de s’asseoir par terre. Il a pris les sept pains et a remercié Dieu pour ce pain. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rompu le pain en morceaux et l’a donné à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples pour qu’ils le distribuent. Et ils l’ont distribué à la foule.

sw.L: Naye anauagiza umati uketi chini; na akiisha kuitwaa ile mikate saba [na] kushukuru, akaimega, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ili waigawe, nao wakaugawia umati.
sw.B: Akauagiza umati wa watu uketi chini. Akaichukua ile mikate saba, akashukuru, akaimega, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waigawe, nao wakawagawia watu.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia watu waketi chini. Akaichukua ile mikate saba, akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili yake. Kisha akaimega vipande vipande, akawapa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawagawie watu. Nao wakawapa watu.

decisions.choice: recline: sit or lie down to eat
decisions.reason: People lay or sat on the ground for a meal, as at the first feeding (6:39-40).

decisions.choice: took, gave thanks, broke, gave: the same actions as at the Last Supper
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same series of verbs at the first feeding (6:41) and at the Last Supper (14:22-23). The word for giving thanks is the one used of the cup at 14:23.

decisions.choice: was giving: he kept handing the bread out
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes repeated action as the bread kept coming.

decisions.choice: thanked God for them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, to whom the thanks were given.

decisions.choice: "ngồi xuống" for "recline"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision gives "sit or lie down to eat"; Vietnamese readers eat sitting, and "nằm" (lie) on the ground would suggest resting, not a meal.

decisions.choice: "감사 기도를 드리다" for giving thanks over the bread
decisions.reason: The thanks is a prayer to God before the meal; "축사하다" is an older church word that new readers would not understand.

decisions.choice: [los]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the object of these verbs unsaid; Spanish needs the pronoun, so Literal brackets it, as English brackets "them".

decisions.choice: "s’allonger" (L), "asseoir" (B, R); "rendre grâce" (L, B), "remercier Dieu" (R)
decisions.reason: As in French John (6:10-11): Literal keeps the verb for reclining at a meal, Balanced and Readable say what the people did. "Rendre grâce" keeps the echo of the Last Supper noted in the meaning decision; Readable says plainly to whom thanks were given.

source.text: καὶ εἶχον ἰχθύδια ὀλίγα· καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτὰ εἶπεν καὶ ταῦτα παρατιθέναι.

records.literal_gloss: And they had small fish a few; and having blessed them he said also these to be set before.

en.L: And they had a few small fish; and having blessed them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to serve these also.
en.B: They also had a few small fish. He blessed them and told the disciples to hand those out too.
en.R: They also had a few small fish. Jesus thanked God for the fish and told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to give them out too.

vi.L: Và họ có ít con cá nhỏ; và chúc phước cho chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo dọn cả những thứ ấy ra nữa.
vi.B: Họ cũng có mấy con cá nhỏ. Ngài chúc phước cho cá, rồi bảo các môn đồ phát luôn cả cá nữa.
vi.R: Họ cũng có vài con cá nhỏ. Đức Giê-xu cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về số cá ấy, rồi bảo các môn đồ phát cá cho mọi người nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들에게 작은 물고기가 몇 마리 있었다. 그분은 그것들을 축복하시고, 이것들도 나누어 주라고 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 또 작은 물고기도 몇 마리 있었다. 예수께서 그것을 두고 감사 기도를 드리시고, 그것도 나누어 주라고 하셨다.
ko.R: 작은 물고기도 몇 마리 있었다. 예수께서는 물고기를 두고도 하나님께 감사드리셨다. 그리고 제자들에게 그것도 나누어 주라고 하셨다.

es.L: Y tenían unos pocos pescaditos; y habiéndolos bendecido, dijo que también estos se sirvieran.
es.B: También tenían unos cuantos pescaditos. Jesús los bendijo y les dijo a los discípulos que también los repartieran.
es.R: También tenían unos pocos pescaditos. Jesús le dio gracias a Dios por los pescados y les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que también los repartieran.

fr.L: Et ils avaient quelques petits poissons ; et, les ayant bénis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit de les servir aussi.
fr.B: Ils avaient aussi quelques petits poissons. Jésus les bénit et dit de les distribuer également.
fr.R: Ils avaient aussi quelques petits poissons. Jésus a remercié Dieu pour les poissons et a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de les distribuer aussi.

sw.L: Na walikuwa na visamaki vichache; naye akiisha kuvibariki, akasema hivi navyo vigawiwe.
sw.B: Walikuwa pia na samaki wadogo wachache. Akawabariki, akawaambia wanafunzi wawagawe hao pia.
sw.R: Walikuwa pia na samaki wadogo wachache. Yesu akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili ya samaki hao, akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawagawe pia.

decisions.choice: blessed them: gave thanks to God over the fish
decisions.reason: In a Jewish blessing at a meal, God is praised for the food. To bless the food means to give thanks for it.

decisions.choice: small fish: little fish, perhaps dried or salted
decisions.reason: The word is a diminutive. Small fish were often dried or pickled around the lake.

decisions.choice: thanked God for the fish
decisions.reason: Readable says what blessing the food means, as in 8:6.

decisions.choice: "chúc phước" (L, B) for "blessed"; "tạ ơn" for "gave thanks" (8:6)
decisions.reason: Mark uses two verbs, "bless" here and "give thanks" in 8:6; Literal and Balanced keep them apart. Readable says what blessing the food meant, thanking God (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "축복하시고" (L); "감사 기도를 드리시고" (B); "하나님께 감사드리셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word "bless"; in Korean "축복하다" sounds like blessing the fish themselves, so Balanced and Readable say that Jesus gave thanks to God over them, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: pescaditos
decisions.reason: The word for small fish, as in John 6:9.

decisions.choice: visamaki (L); samaki wadogo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has a diminutive, "little fish". Literal uses the Swahili diminutive, as John 6:9 does; the other levels say "small fish".

source.text: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν περισσεύματα κλασμάτων ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας.

records.literal_gloss: And they ate and were satisfied, and they took up left over of broken pieces seven large baskets.

en.L: And they ate and were satisfied, and they took up what was left over of broken pieces, seven large baskets.
en.B: Everyone ate and had plenty. Then they collected the leftover pieces, enough to fill seven large baskets.
en.R: All the people ate as much as they wanted. Then the followers picked up the pieces that were left. They filled seven big baskets.

vi.L: Và họ ăn và được no nê, và họ lượm lấy những mẩu bánh còn thừa, được bảy giỏ lớn.
vi.B: Mọi người ăn và được no nê. Rồi họ thu nhặt những mẩu bánh còn thừa, được đầy bảy giỏ lớn.
vi.R: Mọi người ăn bao nhiêu tùy thích. Sau đó các môn đồ nhặt những mẩu bánh còn thừa, được đầy bảy cái giỏ lớn.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 먹고 배불렀다. 그리고 남은 조각들을 거두었는데, 일곱 광주리였다.
ko.B: 사람들은 배불리 먹었다. 그리고 남은 조각을 거두니 일곱 광주리에 가득 찼다.
ko.R: 사람들은 모두 원하는 만큼 배불리 먹었다. 그다음에 제자들이 남은 조각들을 주워 모았다. 그것이 큰 광주리로 일곱 개나 되었다.

es.L: Y comieron y se saciaron, y recogieron lo que sobró de los pedazos: siete canastas grandes.
es.B: Todos comieron hasta quedar satisfechos. Después recogieron los pedazos que sobraron, y llenaron siete canastas grandes.
es.R: Toda la gente comió todo lo que quiso. Después los discípulos recogieron los pedazos que sobraron. Llenaron siete canastas grandes.

fr.L: Et ils mangèrent et furent rassasiés, et ils emportèrent ce qui restait des morceaux : sept grandes corbeilles.
fr.B: Tout le monde mangea à satiété. Puis on ramassa les morceaux qui restaient : de quoi remplir sept grandes corbeilles.
fr.R: Tous les gens ont mangé autant qu’ils voulaient. Ensuite, les disciples ont ramassé les morceaux qui restaient. Ils en ont rempli sept grandes corbeilles.

sw.L: Na wakala, wakashiba, wakaokota mabaki ya vipande, makapu makubwa saba.
sw.B: Watu wote wakala, wakashiba. Kisha wakakusanya vipande vilivyobaki, vikajaza makapu makubwa saba.
sw.R: Watu wote wakala kadiri walivyotaka. Kisha wanafunzi wakaokota vipande vilivyobaki. Wakajaza makapu makubwa saba.

decisions.choice: large baskets: big woven baskets or hampers
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the basket of 6:43 and 8:19. It names a larger basket, big enough to let a man down in it over a wall (Acts 9:25). Jesus keeps the two words apart in 8:19-20.

decisions.choice: satisfied: fed until full
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 6:42 and 8:4.

decisions.choice: large baskets (L, B); big baskets (R)
decisions.reason: The size is part of the meaning of the word. All three levels mark it so that readers can tell these baskets from those of 6:43.

decisions.choice: "giỏ lớn" for this basket, against "giỏ" in 8:19
decisions.reason: Mark names two different baskets for the two feedings, and Jesus repeats the difference in 8:19-20; Vietnamese keeps "giỏ lớn" here and plain "giỏ" there so the reader can see it.

decisions.choice: "광주리" for the large baskets (spyris) here and in 8:20; "바구니" for the baskets (kophinos) of 8:19
decisions.reason: Mark uses two different words for the baskets of the two feedings, and Jesus repeats them in 8:19-20; "광주리" (a large woven basket) and "바구니" keep them apart. "바구니" is also the word of the Korean John 6:13.

decisions.choice: canastas grandes
decisions.reason: Mark uses a different word for the baskets here than at the feeding of the 5000 (meaning decision m1); Spanish keeps the two apart, with "canastas grandes" here and in 8:20, and "cestas" in 8:19, as John 6:13 says.

decisions.choice: "grandes corbeilles" here and in 8:20; "paniers" in 8:19
decisions.reason: Mark uses two different words for the baskets of the two feedings, and Jesus repeats both in 8:19-20 (meaning decisions). French keeps them apart at every level: "paniers", the word of French John 6:13, for the smaller baskets of the five thousand, and "grandes corbeilles" for the large ones here.

decisions.choice: makapu makubwa (large baskets)
decisions.reason: Mark uses a different word for the baskets of the first feeding (6:43; 8:19) and of this one (8:8; 8:20). Swahili keeps them apart: "vikapu" for the smaller baskets, "makapu makubwa" for these large hampers.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ ὡς τετρακισχίλιοι.

records.literal_gloss: There were now about four thousand.

en.L: Now they were about 4,000.
en.B: There were about 4,000 people.
en.R: About 4,000 people were there.

vi.L: Và họ khoảng bốn nghìn [người].
vi.B: Có khoảng bốn nghìn người.
vi.R: Có khoảng bốn nghìn người ở đó.

ko.L: 그런데 그들은 4,000명쯤이었다.
ko.B: 사람은 4,000명쯤 되었다.
ko.R: 그곳에 있던 사람은 4,000명쯤 되었다.

es.L: Y eran unos 4000.
es.B: Eran unas 4000 personas.
es.R: Allí había unas 4000 personas.

fr.L: Or ils étaient environ 4 000.
fr.B: Il y avait là environ 4 000 personnes.
fr.R: Il y avait environ 4 000 personnes.

sw.L: Na walikuwa kama elfu nne.
sw.B: Watu waliokuwapo walikuwa kama elfu nne.
sw.R: Watu wapatao elfu nne walikuwa pale.

decisions.choice: about 4,000: the whole crowd
decisions.reason: Unlike 6:44, the Greek here does not use the word for adult men. It simply counts the crowd.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add the noun that English needs. They use people, since the Greek gives no word for men here.

decisions.choice: "bốn nghìn" in words
decisions.reason: The style guide writes numbers in words in running text; the English uses figures. The same for "năm nghìn" in 8:19 and "bốn nghìn" in 8:20.

decisions.choice: "4,000명" in figures, here and in 8:19-20 ("5,000명")
decisions.reason: Large numbers are written in figures (style guide, section 5), as in the Korean John 6:10.

decisions.choice: elfu nne (four thousand), in words
decisions.reason: The Swahili style writes numbers in words in running text; the English writes the figure.

source.text: καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And he sent away them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them away.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them on their way.
en.R: Then Jesus sent them home.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ về.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ ra về.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu cho họ về nhà.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들을 보내셨다.
ko.B: 그리고 예수께서 그들을 돌려보내셨다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 사람들을 집으로 돌려보내셨다.

es.L: Y los despidió.
es.B: Luego los despidió.
es.R: Luego Jesús los mandó a sus casas.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les renvoya.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les congédia.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus les a renvoyés chez eux.

sw.L: Naye akawaaga.
sw.B: Kisha akawaaga waende zao.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaaga waende nyumbani.

decisions.choice: sent away: dismissed the crowd to go home
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:3. Now they have eaten and can go home.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐμβὰς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having embarked into the boat with the disciples of him he came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

en.L: And immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and came into the region of Dalmanutha.
en.B: At once {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} boarded the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and came to the area of Dalmanutha.
en.R: Right away Jesus got into the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. They went to a place called Dalmanutha.

vi.L: Và lập tức xuống thuyền với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến miền Đa-ma-nu-tha.
vi.B: Ngay sau đó, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ xuống thuyền và đến vùng Đa-ma-nu-tha.
vi.R: Ngay lập tức, Đức Giê-xu cùng các môn đồ xuống thuyền. Họ đi đến một nơi gọi là Đa-ma-nu-tha.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 그분이 자기 제자들과 함께 배에 오르셔서 달마누다 지방으로 가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 곧바로 제자들과 함께 배에 오르셔서 달마누다 지방으로 가셨다.
ko.R: 바로 그 뒤에 예수께서 제자들과 함께 배를 타셨다. 그리고 달마누다라는 곳으로 가셨다.

es.L: Y enseguida, subiendo a la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, fue a la región de Dalmanuta.
es.B: En seguida subió a la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y llegó a la región de Dalmanuta.
es.R: Enseguida Jesús subió a la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Fueron a un lugar llamado Dalmanuta.

fr.L: Et aussitôt, étant monté dans la barque avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint dans la région de Dalmanoutha.
fr.B: Aussitôt, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans la barque avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et se rendit dans la région de Dalmanoutha.
fr.R: Tout de suite après, Jésus est monté dans la barque avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Ils sont allés à un endroit appelé Dalmanoutha.

sw.L: Na mara moja akiingia katika mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, alikuja katika sehemu za Dalmanutha.
sw.B: Mara moja akapanda mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akaenda sehemu za Dalmanutha.
sw.R: Mara moja Yesu akapanda mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Wakaenda mahali paitwapo Dalmanutha.

decisions.choice: Dalmanutha: a place by the lake not known from any other source
decisions.reason: No other ancient writing names Dalmanutha, and where it lay is not known. It was most likely on the west shore of the lake, in Jewish territory, since Pharisees meet Jesus there (8:11).

decisions.choice: Dalmanutha, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read Magadan or Magdala, the names found in the manuscripts of Matthew 15:39. Scribes probably replaced an unknown place with a known one. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a place called Dalmanutha
decisions.reason: Readable signals that Dalmanutha is a place name.

decisions.choice: "Đa-ma-nu-tha"
decisions.reason: The name in the traditional Protestant transliteration, as the style guide sets for names.

decisions.choice: "곧" (L); "곧바로" (B); "바로" (R) for euthys, as in chapters 3 and 7
decisions.reason: Keeps Mark's frequent "immediately" the same through the Korean of the book.

decisions.choice: "달마누다", the Protestant spelling of Dalmanutha
decisions.reason: The settled Protestant forms of names (style guide, Settled).

decisions.choice: enseguida (L, R); en seguida (B)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:10: Literal and Readable keep "enseguida" for Mark's word every time; Balanced uses what reads most naturally.

decisions.choice: "Dalmanoutha"
decisions.reason: The French spelling of the name, with "ou" for the Greek vowel that English writes "u".

decisions.choice: mara moja (immediately)
decisions.reason: Mark's "immediately" is "mara moja", as in Mark 1, so the reader sees how the story moves straight on.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν αὐτῷ, ζητοῦντες παρ’ αὐτοῦ σημεῖον ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And went out the Pharisees and began to argue with him, seeking from him a sign from the heaven, testing him.

en.L: And the Pharisees went out and began to argue with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, seeking from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a sign from heaven, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees came out and started to dispute with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They demanded a sign from heaven, to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the test.
en.R: The Pharisees came out to argue with Jesus. They wanted to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a sign from heaven to prove that God had sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và những người Pha-ri-si đi ra và bắt đầu tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đòi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một dấu lạ từ trời, để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Những người Pha-ri-si đến và bắt đầu tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ đòi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm một dấu lạ từ trời để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Những người Pha-ri-si đến tranh luận với Đức Giê-xu. Họ muốn thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nên đòi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm một dấu lạ từ trời để chứng tỏ rằng Đức Chúa Trời đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến.

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파 사람들이 나와서 그분과 논쟁하기 시작하였다. 그들은 그분을 시험하며 그분에게 하늘로부터 오는 표적을 구하였다.
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들이 와서 예수와 논쟁하기 시작하였다. 그들은 예수를 시험하려고 하늘로부터 오는 표적을 보여 달라고 요구하였다.
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들이 예수께 와서 따지기 시작했다. 그들은 예수를 시험하려고 했다. 그래서 하나님께서 예수를 보내셨다는 것을 증명할 표적을 하늘에서 보여 달라고 했다.

es.L: Y salieron los fariseos y comenzaron a discutir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, pidiéndole una señal del cielo, para ponerlo a prueba.
es.B: Llegaron los fariseos y se pusieron a discutir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Le exigían una señal del cielo, para ponerlo a prueba.
es.R: Los fariseos vinieron a discutir con Jesús. Querían ponerlo a prueba, así que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidieron una señal del cielo que demostrara que Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había enviado.

fr.L: Et les Pharisiens sortirent et commencèrent à discuter avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, cherchant à obtenir de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un signe venant du ciel, pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve.
fr.B: Les Pharisiens vinrent et se mirent à discuter avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandèrent un signe venant du ciel.
fr.R: Les Pharisiens sont venus discuter avec Jésus. Ils voulaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve. Alors ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé un signe venant du ciel, pour prouver que Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait envoyé.

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo walitoka, wakaanza kujadiliana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, wakitafuta kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ishara kutoka mbinguni, wakimjaribu.
sw.B: Mafarisayo walikuja, wakaanza kubishana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Walidai awaonyeshe ishara kutoka mbinguni, ili wamjaribu.
sw.R: Mafarisayo walikuja kubishana na Yesu. Walitaka kumjaribu, kwa hiyo wakamwomba awaonyeshe ishara kutoka mbinguni ili kuthibitisha kwamba Mungu alikuwa amemtuma.

decisions.choice: sign: a sign that would prove God was with him
decisions.reason: In Mark a sign is not one of Jesus' healings, which Mark calls works of power. It is a proof, given on demand, that God backs his claims. Israel asked such signs of God in the wilderness and was blamed for testing him (Psalm 95:8-9).

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: Heaven stands for God himself. The sign would come from the sky, but the point is that God gives it.

decisions.choice: testing: trying to trap him or prove him false
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Satan's testing in 1:13. They want him to fail.

decisions.choice: sign
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term and keeps the same word at every level. Readable explains what the sign was meant to prove.

decisions.choice: "dấu lạ" for "sign"
decisions.reason: The word the Vietnamese John uses for the same Greek noun (style guide section 5). "Phép lạ" (miracle) would lose the sense of proof the Pharisees demand.

decisions.choice: "표적" for sign at every level
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John: a sign that points to God's backing, never simply a "miracle".

decisions.choice: señal
decisions.reason: The word John's Spanish uses for a sign (John 2:11); it points to what the deed shows, as the meaning decision says (m1).

decisions.choice: "mettre à l’épreuve"
decisions.reason: As in French John (6:6, 8:6): "tenter" would suggest tempting to sin; the Pharisees want to test him and catch him out (meaning decision). "Signe", never "miracle", as the English keeps "sign".

decisions.choice: ishara (sign)
decisions.reason: As in John: "ishara" is a sign that points to something; they ask for proof from God, not simply for a wonder.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστενάξας τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ζητεῖ σημεῖον;

records.literal_gloss: And having sighed deeply in the spirit of him he says, Why the generation this seeks a sign?

en.L: And sighing deeply in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Why does this generation seek a sign?
en.B: He groaned from deep within and said, "Why does this generation look for a sign?
en.R: Jesus let out a deep groan and said, "Why do the people of today keep asking for a sign?

vi.L: Và thở dài trong tâm linh mình, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Sao thế hệ này đòi một dấu lạ?
vi.B: Ngài thở dài từ sâu thẳm trong lòng và nói: "Tại sao thế hệ này lại tìm kiếm một dấu lạ?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thở dài não nuột và nói: "Tại sao người đời nay cứ đòi một dấu lạ?

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 자기 영으로 깊이 탄식하시며 말씀하신다. "어찌하여 이 세대가 표적을 구하느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 마음속 깊이 탄식하시며 말씀하셨다. "이 세대가 어찌하여 표적을 구하느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 깊이 한숨을 쉬시며 말씀하셨다. "오늘날 사람들은 왜 자꾸 표적을 달라고 하느냐?

es.L: Y suspirando profundamente en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu, dice: «¿Por qué esta generación busca una señal?
es.B: Dio un gemido desde lo más hondo y dijo: «¿Por qué esta generación pide una señal?
es.R: Jesús dio un profundo gemido y dijo: «¿Por qué la gente de hoy sigue pidiendo una señal?

fr.L: Et, ayant soupiré profondément en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} esprit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Pourquoi cette génération cherche-t-elle un signe ?
fr.B: Il poussa un profond soupir et dit : « Pourquoi cette génération réclame-t-elle un signe ?
fr.R: Jésus a poussé un profond soupir et a dit : « Pourquoi est-ce que les gens d’aujourd’hui demandent toujours un signe ?

sw.L: Naye akiugua sana rohoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, anasema, "Kwa nini kizazi hiki kinatafuta ishara?
sw.B: Akaugua kutoka ndani ya roho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akasema, "Kwa nini watu wa kizazi hiki wanatafuta ishara?
sw.R: Yesu akaugua kwa uchungu, akasema, "Kwa nini watu wa siku hizi wanaendelea kuomba ishara?

decisions.choice: sighed deeply: groaned from the heart
decisions.reason: The verb is stronger than the sigh of 7:34. It shows grief and frustration at their unbelief.

decisions.choice: in his spirit: in his own inner self
decisions.reason: This is Jesus' own spirit, the deepest part of him, as in 2:8.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of this time, seen as unwilling to believe
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the wilderness generation that tested God (Deuteronomy 32:5, 32:20; Psalm 95:10). It comes again in 8:38 and 9:19.

decisions.choice: the people of today
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the word means the people living now.

decisions.choice: "thế hệ này" (L, B); "người đời nay" (R) for "this generation"; likewise in 8:12b and 8:38
decisions.reason: "Thế hệ này" is the modern word for the people of one time; "dòng dõi" now suggests descent. Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "이 세대" (L, B); "오늘날 사람들" (R), here and in 8:38
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the biblical expression; Readable says who is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kizazi hiki (L); watu wa kizazi hiki (B); watu wa siku hizi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kizazi" (generation) means the people living at one time; Balanced says "the people of this generation" so the verb can agree with people, and Readable "the people of these days", as the English Readable says "the people of today".

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ δοθήσεται τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ σημεῖον.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, if will be given to the generation this a sign.

en.L: Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation."
en.B: Truly I tell you, this generation will be given no sign at all."
en.R: I tell you the truth: God will not give them a sign. Never!"

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, sẽ không có dấu lạ nào được ban cho thế hệ này."
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người: thế hệ này sẽ chẳng được ban cho dấu lạ nào cả."
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các người: Đức Chúa Trời sẽ không ban cho họ một dấu lạ nào. Không bao giờ!"

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 이 세대에게는 결코 표적이 주어지지 않을 것이다."
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 이 세대에게는 어떤 표적도 주어지지 않을 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 하나님께서는 이 사람들에게 표적을 보여 주시지 않을 것이다. 절대로!"

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no se dará señal a esta generación».
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a esta generación no se le dará ninguna señal».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: Dios no le dará ninguna señal a esta gente. ¡Nunca!».

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis, aucun signe ne sera donné à cette génération. »
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis : il ne sera donné aucun signe à cette génération. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : Dieu ne leur donnera pas de signe. Jamais ! »

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia, kizazi hiki hakitapewa ishara."
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, kizazi hiki hakitapewa ishara yoyote kamwe."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Mungu hatawapa ishara. Kamwe!"

decisions.choice: if ... a sign: an oath meaning certainly no sign will be given
decisions.reason: This is a Hebrew way of swearing an oath. The full form is "may God punish me if ...", which means "it will certainly not happen" (Psalm 95:11). Jesus denies the demand in the strongest terms.

decisions.choice: will be given: God is the unnamed giver
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God unnamed, as Jewish speech often did.

decisions.choice: no
decisions.reason: Even Literal gives the sense of the oath, since "if" alone would read as an unfinished sentence in English.

decisions.choice: God will not give them a sign. Never!
alternatives: no sign will be given to this generation
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver and shows the force of the oath with a separate word.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R) for the single "Truly I say to you"
alternatives: "Quả thật, Ta nói với các người"
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese John's form for "Truly, truly", said once since Mark has a single "amen"; Readable uses the plain form John's Readable uses. "Các người" because Jesus is speaking to the Pharisees.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The same formula as in the Korean of 3:28 and of John.

decisions.choice: En verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The Spanish of John's "Truly, truly" (John 1:51), with Mark's single "Truly"; a book-wide rendering.

decisions.choice: no se dará
decisions.reason: As in English: the Hebrew-style oath "if a sign will be given" means a firm "no" (meaning decision m1), which Spanish says plainly.

decisions.choice: "En vérité, je vous le dis" (L, B); "Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité" (R)
decisions.reason: Mark’s single "Amen" takes the French form set for John’s double one (French style guide): "En vérité, je vous le dis" at Literal and Balanced, with "le", which French needs and which adds nothing; Readable says it in plain words. Used for Mark as a whole.

decisions.choice: "aucun signe ne sera donné" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek "if a sign will be given" is a Hebrew way of swearing that it will not be given (meaning decision); kept word for word it is not French, so Literal states the denial, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:28: Mark's single "amen" is "Kweli nawaambia", and Readable says "I tell you the truth", as in John.

source.text: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἐμβὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.

records.literal_gloss: And having left them, again having embarked he went away to the other side.

en.L: And leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} again got into [the boat] and went away to the other side.
en.B: Leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat again and went off to the far shore.
en.R: Then Jesus left them. He got back into the boat and went across the lake.

vi.L: Và để họ lại, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại xuống [thuyền] và đi qua bờ bên kia.
vi.B: Ngài bỏ họ lại, xuống thuyền một lần nữa và đi sang bờ bên kia.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu rời bỏ họ. Ngài lại xuống thuyền và đi qua bên kia hồ.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들을 떠나, 다시 [배에] 오르셔서 건너편으로 가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 그들을 떠나 다시 배에 오르셔서 건너편으로 가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 그들을 두고 떠나셨다. 다시 배를 타고 호수 건너편으로 가셨다.

es.L: Y dejándolos, subió otra vez [a la barca] y se fue a la otra orilla.
es.B: Los dejó, volvió a subir a la barca y se fue a la otra orilla.
es.R: Entonces Jesús los dejó. Subió otra vez a la barca y cruzó el lago.

fr.L: Et, les ayant laissés, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} remonta [dans la barque] et s’en alla vers l’autre rive.
fr.B: Il les laissa là, remonta dans la barque et partit vers l’autre rive.
fr.R: Puis Jésus les a quittés. Il est remonté dans la barque et il a traversé le lac.

sw.L: Naye akiwaacha, akapanda [mashua] tena, akaenda zake ng'ambo.
sw.B: Akawaacha, akapanda mashua tena, akaenda ng'ambo ya pili.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaacha. Akapanda mashua tena, akavuka ziwa.

decisions.choice: having left them: Jesus turns his back on the dispute
alternatives: he left them behind by accident
decisions.reason: Leaving them is his answer to their demand.

decisions.choice: the other side: the east shore of the lake
alternatives: another town on the same shore
decisions.reason: They cross back toward the north-east, where they reach Bethsaida (8:22).

decisions.choice: across the lake
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Readable names the lake.

source.text: Καὶ ἐπελάθοντο λαβεῖν ἄρτους, καὶ εἰ μὴ ἕνα ἄρτον οὐκ εἶχον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And they forgot to take loaves, and except one loaf not they had with themselves in the boat.

en.L: And they had forgotten to take loaves, and except for one loaf they did not have [any] with them in the boat.
en.B: Now the disciples had forgotten to bring bread. They had just one loaf with them in the boat.
en.R: Jesus' followers had forgotten to bring any food. They had only one loaf of bread with them in the boat.

vi.L: Và họ đã quên đem theo bánh, và trên thuyền họ không có [bánh] nào với mình ngoài một cái bánh.
vi.B: Các môn đồ đã quên mang theo bánh. Trên thuyền, họ chỉ có một cái bánh.
vi.R: Các môn đồ của Đức Giê-xu đã quên mang theo thức ăn. Trên thuyền, họ chỉ có một ổ bánh.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 빵을 가져오는 것을 잊어버려서, 배 안에 빵 한 개밖에는 가진 것이 없었다.
ko.B: 제자들은 빵 가져오는 것을 잊어버려서, 배 안에는 빵이 한 개밖에 없었다.
ko.R: 제자들은 먹을 것을 가져오는 것을 깜빡 잊었다. 그래서 배 안에는 빵 한 개만 있었다.

es.L: Y se habían olvidado de llevar panes, y no tenían consigo en la barca más que un solo pan.
es.B: Los discípulos se habían olvidado de llevar pan. Solo tenían un pan en la barca.
es.R: Los discípulos de Jesús se habían olvidado de llevar comida. Solo tenían un pan con ellos en la barca.

fr.L: Et ils avaient oublié de prendre des pains, et, sauf un seul pain, ils n’en avaient pas avec eux dans la barque.
fr.B: Or les disciples avaient oublié d’emporter du pain ; ils n’en avaient qu’un seul avec eux dans la barque.
fr.R: Les disciples de Jésus avaient oublié d’emporter de la nourriture. Ils n’avaient qu’un seul pain avec eux dans la barque.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wamesahau kuchukua mikate, na hawakuwa na [mikate] pamoja nao mashuani isipokuwa mkate mmoja.
sw.B: Wanafunzi walikuwa wamesahau kuchukua mikate. Walikuwa na mkate mmoja tu mashuani.
sw.R: Wanafunzi wa Yesu walikuwa wamesahau kuleta chakula. Walikuwa na mkate mmoja tu mashuani.

decisions.choice: they: the disciples
decisions.reason: The disciples are with Jesus in the boat.

decisions.choice: one loaf: perhaps a hint that Jesus himself is the bread they have
alternatives: only a detail of the story
decisions.reason: Mark mentions the single loaf with care. Some read it as pointing to Jesus, who is with them in the boat. Mark does not say so.

decisions.choice: the disciples (B); Jesus' followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since the last people named are the Pharisees.

source.text: καὶ διεστέλλετο αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε, βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῆς ζύμης Ἡρῴδου.

records.literal_gloss: And he was instructing them saying, Watch, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was instructing them, saying, "Watch, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
en.B: He gave them a warning: "Be careful! Watch out for the Pharisees' yeast and Herod's yeast."
en.R: Jesus warned them, "Be careful! Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} răn dặn họ rằng: "Hãy coi chừng, hãy giữ mình khỏi men của người Pha-ri-si và men của Hê-rốt."
vi.B: Ngài cảnh báo họ: "Hãy cẩn thận! Hãy đề phòng men của người Pha-ri-si và men của Hê-rốt."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu cảnh báo các môn đồ: "Các con phải cẩn thận! Hãy coi chừng men của người Pha-ri-si và của Hê-rốt."

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 명령하시며 말씀하셨다. "주의하여라. 바리새파 사람들의 누룩과 헤롯의 누룩을 조심하여라."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 경고하셨다. "조심하여라! 바리새파 사람들의 누룩과 헤롯의 누룩을 경계하여라."
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들에게 주의를 주셨다. "조심하여라! 바리새파 사람들의 누룩과 헤롯의 누룩을 조심하여라."

es.L: Y les daba órdenes, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{plural_you:guárdense|guardaos}} de la levadura de los fariseos y de la levadura de Herodes».
es.B: Les hizo una advertencia: «¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! {{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} de la levadura de los fariseos y de la de Herodes».
es.R: Jesús les advirtió: «¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! {{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} de la levadura de los fariseos y de Herodes».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur faisait des recommandations, disant : « Voyez, prenez garde au levain des Pharisiens et au levain d’Hérode. »
fr.B: Il leur donna cet avertissement : « Attention ! Méfiez-vous du levain des Pharisiens et du levain d’Hérode. »
fr.R: Jésus les a avertis : « Faites attention ! Méfiez-vous du levain des Pharisiens et de celui d’Hérode. »

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaagiza, akisema, "Angalieni, jihadharini na chachu ya Mafarisayo na chachu ya Herode."
sw.B: Akawaonya, "Kuweni macho! Jihadharini na hamira ya Mafarisayo na hamira ya Herode."
sw.R: Yesu akawaonya, "Kuweni waangalifu! Jihadharini na hamira ya Mafarisayo na ya Herode."

decisions.choice: leaven: a bit of old fermented dough used to make new dough rise
decisions.reason: A small piece of old dough spread through a whole batch. In the Scriptures it often stands for a corrupting influence that spreads (1 Corinthians 5:6-8; Exodus 12:15).

decisions.choice: the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod: their unbelief and hostility
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain the picture. The Pharisees have just demanded a sign (8:11), and Herod killed John (6:14-29). The two groups plotted together against Jesus in 3:6. What they share is a refusal to see who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: Herod: Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: The same Herod as in 6:14-29.

decisions.choice: Herod, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "the Herodians", the party of 3:6. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: yeast
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word. Readable keeps the picture, since the disciples' mistake in the next verses depends on it.

decisions.choice: "men" for "leaven" at every level
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has one everyday word for leaven and yeast, so the English difference between the levels does not arise.

decisions.choice: "Hê-rốt" for Herod
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration; "Hê-rô-đê" is the Catholic form.

decisions.choice: "누룩" at every level
decisions.reason: "누룩" is still the everyday Korean word for a leavening starter, it is the word Korean readers know from the Bible, and it keeps the picture of a little that spreads through the whole.

decisions.choice: levadura
decisions.reason: Spanish "levadura" covers both the leaven of the Greek and modern yeast, so one word serves every level.

decisions.choice: "levain" at every level
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "yeast". French "levain" is exactly what the meaning decision describes, a piece of old fermented dough kept to raise the new, and it is still the everyday baker’s word; "levure" is the bought yeast of today.

decisions.choice: chachu (L); hamira (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Galatians 5:9: "chachu" is the older word for leaven, kept at Literal; "hamira" is the everyday word for yeast, as the English Balanced and Readable say "yeast".

source.text: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were reasoning with one another that loaves not they have.

en.L: And they were discussing with one another that they have no loaves.
en.B: They began to talk it over among themselves: they had no bread.
en.R: The followers talked among themselves. They thought Jesus said this because they had not brought any bread.

vi.L: Và họ bàn luận với nhau rằng họ không có bánh.
vi.B: Họ bắt đầu bàn tán với nhau về chuyện không có bánh.
vi.R: Các môn đồ bàn với nhau. Họ nghĩ Đức Giê-xu nói vậy vì họ đã không mang theo bánh.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 자기들에게 빵이 없다고 서로 의논하고 있었다.
ko.B: 제자들은 자기들에게 빵이 없다는 것을 두고 서로 이야기하였다.
ko.R: 제자들은 자기들끼리 이야기를 나누었다. 그들은 자기들이 빵을 가져오지 않아서 예수께서 그런 말씀을 하셨다고 생각했다.

es.L: Y comentaban unos con otros que no tienen panes.
es.B: Ellos se pusieron a comentar entre sí que no tenían pan.
es.R: Los discípulos hablaban entre ellos. Pensaban que Jesús decía eso porque no habían traído pan.

fr.L: Et ils discutaient entre eux de ce qu’ils n’ont pas de pains.
fr.B: Ils se mirent à en parler entre eux : ils n’avaient pas de pain.
fr.R: Les disciples ont parlé entre eux. Ils pensaient que Jésus disait cela parce qu’ils n’avaient pas emporté de pain.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakijadiliana wao kwa wao kwamba hawana mikate.
sw.B: Wakaanza kujadiliana wao kwa wao: hawakuwa na mikate.
sw.R: Wanafunzi wakaanza kuzungumza wao kwa wao. Walidhani Yesu amesema hivyo kwa sababu hawakuleta mikate.

decisions.choice: that they have no loaves: their talk was about having no bread
decisions.reason: The small word can give the content of their talk or its cause. Either way they think Jesus is speaking about real bread.

decisions.choice: they have, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: we have, as their own words
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "saying" and read "we have", making it direct speech. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they thought Jesus said this because
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the disciples misunderstood the warning about yeast.

source.text: καὶ γνοὺς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε;

records.literal_gloss: And having known he says to them, Why are you reasoning that loaves not you have?

en.L: And knowing [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Why are you discussing that you have no loaves?
en.B: Jesus knew what they were saying, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Why are you talking about having no bread?
en.R: Jesus knew what they were talking about. He said to them, "Why are you talking about not having bread?

vi.L: Và biết [điều đó], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Sao các con bàn luận về việc không có bánh?
vi.B: Biết họ đang nói gì, Đức Giê-xu bảo: "Sao các con lại bàn tán về chuyện không có bánh?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu biết họ đang nói về chuyện gì. Ngài nói với họ: "Sao các con lại nói chuyện về việc không có bánh?

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 알아차리시고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희는 어찌하여 빵이 없다고 의논하느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 그것을 아시고 말씀하셨다. "어찌하여 너희는 빵이 없다는 이야기를 하고 있느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서는 제자들이 무슨 이야기를 하는지 아셨다. 그래서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "왜 빵이 없다는 이야기를 하느냐?

es.L: Y dándose cuenta, les dice: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:comentan|comentáis}} que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} panes?
es.B: Jesús se dio cuenta de lo que decían y les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hablan|habláis}} de que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} pan?
es.R: Jesús supo de qué estaban hablando. Les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:están|estáis}} hablando de que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} pan?

fr.L: Et, [le] sachant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Pourquoi discutez-vous de ce que vous n’avez pas de pains ?
fr.B: Jésus savait ce qu’ils disaient, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Pourquoi parlez-vous de ce que vous n’avez pas de pain ?
fr.R: Jésus savait de quoi ils parlaient. Il leur a dit : « Pourquoi est-ce que vous parlez du pain que vous n’avez pas ?

sw.L: Naye akitambua, anawaambia, "Kwa nini mnajadiliana kwamba hamna mikate?
sw.B: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakisema, akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnazungumza juu ya kutokuwa na mikate?
sw.R: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakizungumza. Akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnazungumza juu ya kukosa mikate?

decisions.choice: knowing it: he was aware of their talk
decisions.reason: Mark does not say how he knew. In 2:8 Jesus knows people's thoughts in his spirit.

decisions.choice: why: a rebuke, not a request for information
decisions.reason: This and the questions that follow scold the disciples for missing the point.

source.text: οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ συνίετε;

records.literal_gloss: Not yet do you perceive nor understand?

en.L: Do you not yet perceive or understand?
en.B: Do you still not see it or understand?
en.R: Do you still not understand?

vi.L: Các con vẫn chưa nhận biết, cũng chưa hiểu sao?
vi.B: Các con vẫn chưa thấy, chưa hiểu sao?
vi.R: Các con vẫn chưa hiểu sao?

ko.L: 아직도 알지 못하고 깨닫지 못하느냐?
ko.B: 아직도 알아보지 못하고 깨닫지 못하느냐?
ko.R: 아직도 깨닫지 못하느냐?

es.L: ¿Todavía no {{plural_you:perciben|percibís}} ni {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?
es.B: ¿Todavía no lo {{plural_you:ven|veis}} ni lo {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?
es.R: ¿Todavía no {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}?

fr.L: Ne saisissez-vous pas encore, et ne comprenez-vous pas ?
fr.B: Vous ne voyez pas encore, vous ne comprenez pas ?
fr.R: Vous ne comprenez toujours pas ?

sw.L: Bado hamtambui wala hamwelewi?
sw.B: Bado hamwoni wala hamwelewi?
sw.R: Bado hamwelewi?

decisions.choice: perceive, understand: the words of Isaiah 6:9-10, used of outsiders in 4:12
decisions.reason: In 4:12 Jesus used these words of those outside, who see but do not perceive. Now he asks whether his own disciples are in the same state.

decisions.choice: understand
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two verbs, which mean nearly the same, into one plain word.

source.text: πεπωρωμένην ἔχετε τὴν καρδίαν ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Hardened have you the heart of you?

en.L: Do you have your heart hardened?
en.B: Have your hearts been hardened?
en.R: Are your hearts so hard that you cannot understand?

vi.L: Lòng các con bị cứng cỏi sao?
vi.B: Lòng các con đã chai cứng rồi sao?
vi.R: Lòng các con cứng cỏi đến nỗi không thể hiểu được sao?

ko.L: 너희 마음이 굳어져 있느냐?
ko.B: 너희 마음이 그렇게 굳어 있느냐?
ko.R: 너희 마음이 그렇게 굳어서 깨닫지 못하느냐?

es.L: ¿{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} endurecido {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón?
es.B: ¿{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} el corazón endurecido?
es.R: ¿Tan duro {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} el corazón que no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} entender?

fr.L: Avez-vous votre cœur endurci ?
fr.B: Votre cœur est-il endurci ?
fr.R: Votre cœur est-il si dur que vous ne pouvez pas comprendre ?

sw.L: Mna moyo wenu uliofanywa mgumu?
sw.B: Je, mioyo yenu imekuwa migumu?
sw.R: Je, mioyo yenu ni migumu kiasi kwamba hamwezi kuelewa?

decisions.choice: hardened: dull and closed to understanding
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thinking. Mark said this of the disciples after Jesus walked on the water (6:52), and of Jesus' opponents in 3:5.

decisions.choice: so hard that you cannot understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what a hard heart means here, as at 6:52.

decisions.choice: "votre cœur", singular, at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek has the singular, the heart of the group, and French says it the same way; the English Balanced and Readable use the plural.

decisions.choice: moyo wenu (L, singular); mioyo yenu (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:5: Literal keeps the Greek singular "heart" for the group; Balanced and Readable use the plural, the natural Swahili for many people.

source.text: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες οὐ βλέπετε καὶ ὦτα ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούετε;

records.literal_gloss: Eyes having not do you see, and ears having not do you hear?

en.L: Having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear?
en.B: You have eyes; can you not see? You have ears; can you not hear?
en.R: You have eyes, but you do not see! You have ears, but you do not hear!

vi.L: Có mắt mà các con không thấy, và có tai mà các con không nghe sao?
vi.B: Các con có mắt, sao không thấy? Có tai, sao không nghe?
vi.R: Các con có mắt mà không thấy! Có tai mà không nghe!

ko.L: 눈이 있으면서도 보지 못하고, 귀가 있으면서도 듣지 못하느냐?
ko.B: 너희는 눈이 있어도 보지 못하느냐? 귀가 있어도 듣지 못하느냐?
ko.R: 너희는 눈이 있어도 보지 못하는구나! 귀가 있어도 듣지 못하는구나!

es.L: Teniendo ojos, ¿no {{plural_you:ven|veis}}? Y teniendo oídos, ¿no {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}?
es.B: {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} ojos, ¿y no {{plural_you:ven|veis}}? {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} oídos, ¿y no {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}?
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} ojos, pero no {{plural_you:ven|veis}}! ¡{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} oídos, pero no {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}!

fr.L: Ayant des yeux, ne voyez-vous pas, et ayant des oreilles, n’entendez-vous pas ?
fr.B: Vous avez des yeux : ne voyez-vous pas ? Vous avez des oreilles : n’entendez-vous pas ?
fr.R: Vous avez des yeux, mais vous ne voyez pas ! Vous avez des oreilles, mais vous n’entendez pas !

sw.L: Mkiwa na macho hamwoni, na mkiwa na masikio hamsikii?
sw.B: Mna macho; je, hamwezi kuona? Mna masikio; je, hamwezi kusikia?
sw.R: Mna macho, lakini hamwoni! Mna masikio, lakini hamsikii!

decisions.choice: eyes that do not see, ears that do not hear: the prophets' charge against Israel
decisions.reason: The words recall Jeremiah 5:21 and Ezekiel 12:2, where God's people have eyes and ears but will not use them. They also echo 4:9 and 4:12. The healings of a deaf man (7:31-37) and a blind man (8:22-26) stand on either side of this scene.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer that they do not see or hear. Readable says this plainly.

decisions.choice: two questions (L)
decisions.reason: Spanish opens and closes each question with its own marks, so Literal sets the Greek's single question as two that follow its order.

source.text: καὶ οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους ἔκλασα εἰς τοὺς πεντακισχιλίους, πόσους κοφίνους κλασμάτων πλήρεις ἤρατε;

records.literal_gloss: And not do you remember, \v 19 when the five loaves I broke for the five thousand, how many baskets of broken pieces full you took up?

en.L: And do you not remember, \v 19 when I broke the five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets full of broken pieces you took up?"
en.B: Do you not remember? \v 19 When I broke five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets of leftover pieces did you gather?"
en.R: Do you not remember? \v 19 I broke five loaves of bread for 5,000 people. How many baskets of leftover pieces did you pick up?"

vi.L: Và các con không nhớ sao, \v 19 khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bẻ năm cái bánh cho năm nghìn [người], các con đã lượm được bao nhiêu giỏ đầy những mẩu bánh?"
vi.B: Các con không nhớ sao? \v 19 Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bẻ năm cái bánh cho năm nghìn người, các con đã thu được bao nhiêu giỏ đầy bánh thừa?"
vi.R: Các con không nhớ sao? \v 19 Ta đã bẻ năm ổ bánh cho năm nghìn người ăn. Các con đã nhặt được bao nhiêu giỏ bánh thừa?"

ko.L: 그리고 기억하지 못하느냐? \v 19 내가 빵 다섯 개를 떼어 5,000명에게 [주었을] 때, 조각을 가득 담은 바구니를 몇 개나 거두었느냐?"
ko.B: 기억하지 못하느냐? \v 19 내가 빵 다섯 개를 떼어 5,000명에게 나누어 주었을 때, 남은 조각을 몇 바구니나 거두었느냐?"
ko.R: 기억나지 않느냐? \v 19 내가 빵 다섯 개를 떼어서 5,000명을 먹였다. 그때 너희가 남은 조각을 주워 담은 바구니가 몇 개였느냐?"

es.L: ¿Y no {{plural_you:recuerdan|recordáis}}, \v 19 cuando partí los cinco panes para los 5000, cuántas cestas llenas de pedazos {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:recuerdan|recordáis}}? \v 19 Cuando partí cinco panes para los 5000, ¿cuántas cestas de pedazos sobrantes {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.R: ¿No {{plural_you:se acuerdan|os acordáis}}? \v 19 Yo partí cinco panes para 5000 personas. ¿Cuántas cestas de pedazos sobrantes {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».

fr.L: Et ne vous souvenez-vous pas, \v 19 quand j’ai rompu les cinq pains pour les 5 000, combien de paniers pleins de morceaux vous avez emportés ? »
fr.B: Ne vous souvenez-vous pas ? \v 19 Quand j’ai rompu les cinq pains pour les 5 000, combien de paniers de morceaux avez-vous ramassés ? »
fr.R: Vous ne vous rappelez pas ? \v 19 J’ai rompu cinq pains pour 5 000 personnes. Combien de paniers de morceaux qui restaient avez-vous ramassés ? »

sw.L: Na hamkumbuki, \v 19 nilipoimega ile mikate mitano kwa wale elfu tano, mliokota vikapu vingapi vilivyojaa vipande?"
sw.B: Je, hamkumbuki? \v 19 Nilipoimega mikate mitano kwa watu elfu tano, mlikusanya vikapu vingapi vya vipande vilivyobaki?"
sw.R: Je, hamkumbuki? \v 19 Niliimega mikate mitano kwa ajili ya watu elfu tano. Mliokota vikapu vingapi vya vipande vilivyobaki?"

decisions.choice: do you not remember: read as running into the question of 8:19
alternatives: a separate question ending at the end of 8:18
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates 8:18 and 8:19 as one question. Some editions end the question at "remember". The sense does not change.

decisions.choice: baskets: the smaller baskets of the first feeding
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the word of 6:43 here and the word for large baskets in 8:20. Mark keeps the two feedings apart.

decisions.choice: I broke: Jesus names himself as the one who provided
decisions.reason: The point of the questions is who fed the crowds, and that he is with them in the boat.

decisions.choice: 5,000 people
decisions.reason: Readable adds people, as English needs a noun. In 6:44 the count was of men.

decisions.choice: cestas
decisions.reason: The baskets of the first feeding (meaning decision m2), the word of John 6:13; the large baskets of 8:8 and 8:20 are "canastas grandes".

decisions.choice: vikapu (baskets)
decisions.reason: The smaller baskets of the first feeding, kept apart from the large "makapu" of 8:8 and 8:20, as Mark keeps his two words apart.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δώδεκα.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, Twelve.

en.L: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Twelve."
en.B: "Twelve," they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They answered, "Twelve."

vi.L: Họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Mười hai."
vi.B: "Mười hai giỏ," họ thưa.
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Mười hai giỏ."

ko.L: 그들이 그분께 말한다. "열둘입니다."
ko.B: "열두 바구니입니다" 하고 그들이 대답하였다.
ko.R: 제자들이 대답했다. "열두 바구니였습니다."

es.L: Le dicen: «Doce».
es.B: «Doce», {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron.
es.R: Ellos contestaron: «Doce».

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Douze. »
fr.B: « Douze », {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent-ils.
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Douze. »

sw.L: Wanamwambia, "Kumi na viwili."
sw.B: "Kumi na viwili," wakamjibu.
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Kumi na viwili."

decisions.choice: they say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 8:1, the sense is past.

decisions.choice: "thưa" for the disciples answering Jesus (also 8:4, 8:5, 8:20, 8:28-29)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks a younger person or follower speaking to a teacher with "thưa", as the Vietnamese John does for the disciples; Readable uses the plain "trả lời".

source.text: ὅτε καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ εἰς τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους, πόσων σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων ἤρατε;

records.literal_gloss: When the seven for the four thousand, of how many large baskets fillings of broken pieces you took up?

en.L: "When [I broke] the seven for the 4,000, how many large baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?"
en.B: "And when I broke seven loaves for the 4,000, how many large baskets of pieces did you gather?"
en.R: "And when I broke seven loaves for 4,000 people, how many big baskets of leftover pieces did you pick up?"

vi.L: "Còn khi [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bẻ] bảy [cái bánh] cho bốn nghìn [người], các con đã lượm được bao nhiêu giỏ lớn đầy những mẩu bánh?"
vi.B: "Còn khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bẻ bảy cái bánh cho bốn nghìn người, các con đã thu được bao nhiêu giỏ lớn đầy bánh thừa?"
vi.R: "Còn khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bẻ bảy ổ bánh cho bốn nghìn người ăn, các con đã nhặt được bao nhiêu giỏ lớn bánh thừa?"

ko.L: "[내가] 일곱 개를 4,000명에게 [떼어 주었을] 때에는, 조각을 가득 담은 광주리를 몇 개나 거두었느냐?"
ko.B: "또 내가 빵 일곱 개를 떼어 4,000명에게 나누어 주었을 때, 남은 조각을 몇 광주리나 거두었느냐?"
ko.R: "그리고 내가 빵 일곱 개를 떼어서 4,000명을 먹였을 때, 너희가 남은 조각을 주워 담은 큰 광주리가 몇 개였느냐?"

es.L: «Y cuando [partí] los siete para los 4000, ¿cuántas canastas grandes llenas de pedazos {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.B: «Y cuando partí los siete panes para los 4000, ¿cuántas canastas grandes de pedazos {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».
es.R: «Y cuando partí siete panes para 4000 personas, ¿cuántas canastas grandes de pedazos sobrantes {{plural_you:recogieron|recogisteis}}?».

fr.L: « Quand [j’ai rompu] les sept pour les 4 000, combien de grandes corbeilles pleines de morceaux avez-vous emportées ? »
fr.B: « Et quand j’ai rompu les sept pains pour les 4 000, combien de grandes corbeilles de morceaux avez-vous ramassées ? »
fr.R: « Et quand j’ai rompu sept pains pour 4 000 personnes, combien de grandes corbeilles de morceaux qui restaient avez-vous ramassées ? »

sw.L: "Na [nilipoimega] ile saba kwa wale elfu nne, mliokota makapu makubwa mangapi yaliyojaa vipande?"
sw.B: "Na nilipoimega mikate saba kwa watu elfu nne, mlikusanya makapu makubwa mangapi ya vipande?"
sw.R: "Na nilipoimega mikate saba kwa ajili ya watu elfu nne, mliokota makapu makubwa mangapi ya vipande vilivyobaki?"

decisions.choice: when the seven for the 4,000: the verb broke is understood from 8:19
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the question in short form for the second feeding.

decisions.choice: large baskets: the word of 8:8
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same word for each meal that Mark used in telling it.

decisions.choice: I broke (L in brackets); loaves (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs the verb and the noun that the short question leaves out.

source.text: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἑπτά.

records.literal_gloss: And they say to him, Seven.

en.L: And they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Seven."
en.B: "Seven," they said.
en.R: They answered, "Seven."

vi.L: Và họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Bảy."
vi.B: "Bảy giỏ," họ thưa.
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Bảy giỏ."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그분께 말한다. "일곱입니다."
